elements.quote: Stroke is the most common cause of complex disability. 1 Neuropsychiatric symptoms are often associated with stroke; among them, depression is the most prevalent. Prevalence of major depression in people after stroke is 25% at the acute stage and 31% at 3 months poststroke 2 ; however, few individuals receive effective management for depressive symptoms post-stroke. 3 ... Three meta-analyses have been conducted to provide synthesized evidence on the effectiveness of pharmacological interventions for depressive symptoms following stroke, but results were mixed. 5,6,9 ... However, none of these reviews quantitatively demonstrated the effectiveness of different types of NPIs.
elements.reason: The text describes the prevalence and impact of post-stroke depression, notes the mixed results of existing pharmacological meta-analyses, and highlights the lack of quantitative evidence for non-pharmacological interventions, thereby describing the current state of knowledge and uncertainties.

elements.quote: Unaddressed depressive symptoms can lead to devastating effects... For these reasons, an alternative, or addition, to pharmaceutical options is essential to ensure effective management of depressive symptoms after stroke. ... Therefore, to address this research gap, this study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis to synthesize and compare the available evidence regarding the effectiveness of various NPIs for treating depression in people following stroke.
elements.reason: The text explains the negative consequences of unaddressed depression, the limitations of pharmacological options, and explicitly states the study's aim to address the research gap, explaining the importance and need for the review.

elements.quote: Three meta-analyses have been conducted to provide synthesized evidence on the effectiveness of pharmacological interventions for depressive symptoms following stroke, but results were mixed. 5,6,9 ... Three reviews have identified several NPIs for post-stroke depression and have qualitatively provided evidence. 8,11,14 ... However, none of these reviews quantitatively demonstrated the effectiveness of different types of NPIs. Therefore, to address this research gap, this study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis...
elements.reason: The text identifies existing systematic reviews (citing authors like Chen et al., Hackett et al.), explains the limitations of those reviews (mixed results, qualitative only), and justifies the current review as a quantitative synthesis to fill that gap.

The text defines NPIs as 'science-based and non-invasive interventions' but does not describe the specific biological or psychological mechanism of action by which these interventions ameliorate depressive symptoms.
There is no mention of a logic model or hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes in the provided Introduction text.

elements.quote: Objective: To compare the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions on depressive symptoms in people after stroke.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the objective of the review.

elements.quote: The PICOS (Participants, Interventions, Comparisons, Outcomes, Study Designs) checklist was used to identify the inclusion criteria in this review.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the use of the PICOS framework to define inclusion criteria, detailing Participants, Interventions, Comparisons, Outcomes, and Study Designs.

elements.quote: The PICOS (Participants, Interventions, Comparisons, Outcomes, Study Designs) checklist was used to identify the inclusion criteria in this review. 17 Participants (P): This review included trials if they targeted persons with stroke (ischemic and hemorrhagic), regardless of comorbidities and any previous treatments, but excluded those with manic or psychotic episodes/symptoms in order to reduce biases associated with non-target symptoms. Participants were included whether or not they received pharmacological interventions (any dosage or duration) for depression or other illnesses. Interventions (I) and controls (C): This review considered trials that compared the effects of NPIs for post-stroke individuals with depressive symptoms (eg, music therapy, massage therapy, behavioral therapy, or physical exercise with any frequency, intensity, or duration) to control conditions, such as usual treatment. Outcomes (O): The primary outcome of this review was depressive symptoms, measured by any validated depression scale. Study designs (S): This review considered any RCT with a pre-post design, meaning that outcomes were measured at pre-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up.
elements.reason: The study explicitly specifies all PICOS components, including participants (stroke), interventions (NPIs), comparisons (control), outcomes (depressive symptoms), and study designs (RCT with pre-post/follow-up).

elements.quote: The search was restricted to randomized controlled trials (RCTs) written in English and published in peer-reviewed journals.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies language (English) and publication status (peer-reviewed journals). The dissemination year (January 2000 to August 2018) is specified in text_5.

The manuscript states 25 articles were excluded for not meeting inclusion criteria but does not explicitly distinguish between exclusion due to outcomes not being measured versus outcomes not being reported.
